grammar.point: Verbs for money: cost, spend, save, afford
grammar.point_ko: 돈 관련 동사: cost, spend, save, afford
grammar.explanation_en: 'Cost' takes a thing as subject ('This bag costs 50 dollars'). 'Spend' takes a person as subject and money as object ('I spent 50 dollars'). 'Save' means to keep money for later, and 'afford' means having enough money to buy something, often used with 'can/can't'.
grammar.explanation_ko: 'cost'는 물건이 주어입니다('This bag costs 50 dollars'). 'spend'는 사람이 주어이고 돈이 목적어입니다('I spent 50 dollars'). 'save'는 나중을 위해 돈을 모으는 것이고, 'afford'는 살 만한 여유가 있다는 뜻으로 보통 'can/can't'와 함께 씁니다.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 새 차를 살 여유가 없어요.

reading.title: Saving Money
reading.text: I want to buy a new laptop, but it costs 1,200 dollars. I can't afford it right now, so I decided to save money every month. I spend less on coffee and eating out. If I save 100 dollars a month, I will have enough money in a year.
reading.text_ko: 저는 새 노트북을 사고 싶은데, 1,200달러예요. 지금은 살 여유가 없어서 매달 돈을 모으기로 했어요. 커피와 외식에 돈을 덜 써요. 한 달에 100달러씩 모으면 1년 안에 충분한 돈이 생길 거예요.

explanation.en: The text says 'I spend less on coffee and eating out.'
The text says 'If I save 100 dollars a month.'
